newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on Chubais appointment.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on Chubais appointment.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Tuesday in early trade on local and foreign buying encouraged by the appointment of Anatoly Chubais as First Deputy Prime Minister, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares opened at 317.28 after 316.89 at Friday's close. Markets were closed on Monday.
"Even before the market opened we were stormed with calls from big foreign investors," said IK Prospekt corporate securities director Andrei Ippolitov. "I have not seen any rouble purchases yet."
On Friday President Boris Yeltsin appointed his liberal aide Chubais to the post of first deputy prime minister. Traders were unanimous in saying it was good news for the market.
"Chubais is a progressive person and the father of Russian privatisation," Ippolitov said, forecasting a 10 percent rise this week.
Trinfiko senior trader Grigory Pinsky said foreign investors were very much encouraged by the news, but said he saw no foreign purchases yet.
"Foreigners stopped agressive buying and it is enough for our brokers to start pushing the market up," he said.

But Boris Shvedsky, an IK Aton broker, said foreign buying was focused on second-tier oil, energy and telecommunication stocks, and Rostelekom RTKM.RTS, while Russian operators bought other leading shares.

At 0820 GMT Rostelekom edged up to $4.10 from $4.00 at Friday's close, utility UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2250 from $0.2165, LUKoil LKOH.RTS was $14.43 after $13.84 and Norilsk Nickel rose to $6.75 from $6.55.
